name: Honeydew
lede: Honeydew is a very pale green, a web-standard color name that shares a word with the melon, the sweet insect secretion, and an older pinkish tint.

sections.title: Two colors, one word
sections.body:
Paterson lists two entries. Lower-case honeydew is a yellowy pink or orangey pink, while capitalized Honeydew is a pale green, one of the colors in the X11 set, with the hex code #F0FFF0 [1]. The index files honeydew under pinks and Honeydew under greens, with the asterisk Paterson uses for X11 names [2][3][4]. So the same word names two different colors, which is why a digital swatch here should not be read as an older color name.

The X11 value #F0FFF0 is nearly white with a green tint [1]. Nearby names are [[mint-cream]], [[pistachio]] and [[celadon]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch matches 15 of 23,781 archive paintings (0.06%, as photographed), rarer than 69% of the named colors [5]. The earliest dated match is a painting by Piero della Francesca from 1470, and the latest is 1891, among 11 dated paintings; the early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [5]. In printed English the word, in its adjective use, peaks in the 1980s and rose fastest in the 1930s [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so the match is not a pigment test.
